subject: secrdesign: extracting raw datasets with a group structure

messages.author: 72f2ccabe1e5089f
messages.subject: secrdesign: extracting raw datasets with a group structure
parts:
Hi Murray
You may recall that I am working on design issues using secrdesign. I have just tried to use fit = FALSE (with extractfn = identity) so I could look at the datasets being simulated for a scenario with different trap arrays but got the following error:

Error in run.scenarios(scen, trapset = traps.list, nrepl = nreps, extractfn = identity,  :  
  Fields trapsindexnoccasionsnrepeatsfitindexmaskindex must be constant across groups

Does this mean that I can only extract datasets for the same trap (and mask) layout?

Many thanks

Greg

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: secrdesign: extracting raw datasets with a group structure
parts:
Greg
I think I've found where the wheels come off, pending your scenario data.frame.

If you specify group-specific sigma AND leave run.scenarios to construct the maskset THEN maskindex varies between groups within a scenario, which is not allowed. This can be fixed by specifying the masks (they can still differ between scenarios). I've added a more detailed error message to the code on GitHub that you can install with devtools::install_github("MurrayEfford/secrdesign") (if brave).

Murray

For example:
library(secrdesign)
scen <- make.scenarios(D = 5, trapsindex = 1:3, sigma = 25, g0 = 0.2, groups = 1:2)
scen$sigma <- c(20,30)[scen$group]  # group-specific sigma
traplist <- rep(list(make.grid()), 3)

# fails
sims <- run.scenarios(nrepl = 10, scenarios = scen, trapset = traplist,
                      ncores = 1, extractfn = identity)
# runs
scen$maskindex <- rep(1,nrow(scen))
masklist <- list(make.mask(traplist[[1]], buffer=100))
sims <- run.scenarios(nrepl = 10, scenarios = scen, trapset = traplist,
                      maskset = masklist, ncores = 1, extractfn = identity)

messages.author: 72f2ccabe1e5089f
messages.subject: Re: secrdesign: extracting raw datasets with a group structure
parts:
Thanks Murray. I have explicitly provided the maskset and am no longer getting an error when extracting the raw data. I was initially getting a warning message when using fit.models to try fit models to the raw data (saying that only one group is being summarised) but when I changed the extractfn from the default (which is NULL for fit.models) to predict it then worked.

Many thanks as always

Greg
